cli.tool: hf download (huggingface_hub 1.26.0, hf_xet backend), weights only, fresh cache, writes to disk, 1 rep
cli.note: nic_rx < bytes written = Xet chunk dedup/compression on the wire (~8-10% on 7B/9B)

provenance.data_path: 100% of 449 data requests served by us.aws.cdn.hf.co = HF's OWN CDN/Xet bridge (x-hf-cdn-pop: aws-us-east-1). NOT CloudFront (no cloudfront.net CNAME, no Via/X-Cache; plain A records to EC2 us-east-1). NOT direct S3 (S3 origin hidden behind the bridge).
provenance.control_plane: huggingface.co /resolve hop IS CloudFront-fronted; every redirect was 'X-Cache: Miss from cloudfront' (per-request signed URLs, uncacheable by design), POP IAD55.
provenance.edge_warmth: rep2 vs rep1 on 3 representatives: TTFB 498 vs 640 ms, per-stream 32 vs 28 MiB/s - mild (~10-20%), consistent with a large always-warm regional fleet, not a thin edge cache over S3.
provenance.cli_route_equivalence: Verified by observing a live CLI download's TCP peers (ss sampling) plus the xet-read-token API: the CLI gets casUrl=cas-server.xethub.hf.co (EC2, chunk metadata) and pulls chunk DATA from us.aws.cdn.hf.co - the SAME fleet the /resolve tracer hit. The CloudFront-fronted xet hosts (transfer/cas-bridge.xethub.hf.co, Server: CloudFront, POP IAD55) exist but were NOT contacted for this anonymous download; the token carries hfCdnTier=unauthenticated, so authenticated/other tiers may route differently.

paired_probe_same_window.conclusion: Harness numbers (both ours and HF CLI) are capped ~135 MiB/s by the CLIENT's verify + EBS-write pipeline, not the NIC (burst was active: 590 MiB/s receive demonstrated). Transport-only, the i4i cache is 2.4x faster than HF's bridge to the same client.
paired_probe_same_window.cli_warm_rerun_note: Stock CLI re-run on SimPO AFTER the bridge had served it in full 4x within the hour (maximally warm): 154.1 s vs the original 149.7 s. Cache state contributes nothing measurable to CLI numbers - the CLI is client-side limited (chunk verify + disk writes + its own concurrency). Rules out the 'first run was cold origin' interpretation.
